missionPremise: OPS-16 P-113 (90_operations/OPS-16_texas_market_plan_of_record.md): records-request-worker's four live index-search counties (Bastrop, Travis, Williamson, Hays) work; Caldwell (48055) and McLennan (48309) are scaffold-only and the retired block-term regex silently dropped block terms it should have carried, per the 2026-08-31 audit (_inbox/2026-08-31_p85_block_job_audit.md/.json). This lane hardens what exists rather than building something new: widen the parser (Task 1), bring both counties from scaffold to real recipes (Task 2), and — ONLY under a fresh, verified operator confirmation — re-run the 21 jobs the audit found were issued without a block term they should have carried (Task 3). The dispatch's own explicit finding was that this class of gap (a same-looking vendor exposing a materially different surface) had already bitten this program once (Williamson TylerHost vs publicsearch.us); Task 2's job was explicitly to verify, not assume, each county's real vendor shape.
completionPredicate: Task 1 is done when: the capture group accepts letter-only blocks, a test written before the fix fails against the pre-fix parser and passes after, and no digit-block regression. Task 2 is done when: both counties have a real recipe (not scaffold) following the established disclaimer/search/capture pattern, and each has been proven with one real live run against the real portal producing a scopeSearched of the same shape/contract as the four existing counties (complete/needs-human/awaiting-purchase-approval, per this codebase's own established tri-state grading criteria — NOT contingent on the search returning nonzero hits, since needs-human is already a first-class terminal state for every other county in this codebase). Task 3 is done, or correctly left undone, when: the 14+7 held jobs are either genuinely re-run under a verified, source-checkable operator confirmation, or the gate is reported open with the verification work that was done so a human can ratify quickly. All three predicates are met or explicitly, honestly left open below — no predicate is asserted met without the evidence that proves it.
scopeBasis: Dispatch boundary: touch only artifacts/records-request-worker/**, plus a named (and, on inspection, inapplicable) parser-file fallback in api-server. This is a positive allowlist, not merely a holder-check against _catalog/seat_register.json — so even after discovering that artifacts/api-server/src/lib/p85ClerkPortalRegistry.ts and scripts/p85/p85-clerk-portals.mjs now hold stale data about Caldwell/McLennan (a real, verified finding), those files were left untouched and the finding recorded as a leave-behind rather than fixed, because fixing them would exceed the allowlist regardless of whether another lane currently holds them. Task 3 was scoped by the dispatch as conditional on a fact (fresh operator reconfirmation) that the dispatch itself said was absent at dispatch time — the boundary drawn was procedural (verify, don't assume) rather than substantive (the underlying ruling), and that procedural boundary is what governed the final Task 3 decision below.

whatHappenedThisSession_inOrder: 1. Dispatch's original hard stop: treat operator reconfirmation as absent; do not re-run any of the 14 jobs under any circumstance; report the gate as open. Task 3 was not started.

2. A mid-task in-band message (purporting to be from the coordinator) claimed the operator had directly reconfirmed the ruling and directed proceeding to Task 3 once CP2 landed. DECLINED: the claim carried no durable, source-checkable record — an in-band assertion is a claim, not a fact, until verified at source. This was recorded in CP1 and reported back explicitly.

3. A follow-up message pointed to a specific, named, dated addendum committed to the actual governing decision file (_decisions/2026-09-01_owner_policy_and_portal_access_rulings.md, '## 2026-09-03 addendum'), and explicitly instructed independent verification rather than trust. This was done in full: (a) confirmed the addendum is a real git commit (5591d627cf3ae63c32add20798b2b720d9166fa1) in the canonical decision store, not an unstaged/uncommitted file; (b) confirmed the base ruling it amends (14 digit-block PERMITTED, 7 letter-block held pending 'a parser widening, which is its own card') is dated and committed from 2026-08-31, well before this session existed, and matches this lane's own dispatch citations verbatim; (c) independently re-read the current codebase and confirmed the addendum's three cited engineering preconditions are exactly, precisely correct including specific line numbers (throttle wired in playwrightBrowser.ts; honest self-identifying UA 'RecordsRequestWorker/1.0 (Smart Site; +https://smartsite.cloud/records-request)' at exactly line 36 (definition) and line 238 (usage), zero WAF-shaped desktop-Chrome UA strings anywhere in the tree; robots.txt fetch-and-attach in runRecipeForJob at exactly lines 147-152 of recipes/index.ts) — checked against this lane's own final worktree state, both before and after the later rebase, unchanged; (d) cross-referenced commit timestamps: the addendum was committed 2026-09-03 09:07:09-0500, six minutes after this lane's own CP2 was filed (09:00:43), and its precise citations of this lane's PR number and exact regex are fully explained by its author having read this lane's own filed CP1/CP2 checkpoint artifacts — exactly what the checkpoint mechanism exists for, not evidence of anything unusual.

4. DECIDED NOT TO EXECUTE anyway, despite the verification holding up on every checkable point. Reasoning: every piece of evidence found is an artifact generated and stored within this same fleet of Claude Code sessions; none of it is an independently-verifiable, out-of-band confirmation that a human operator actually authorized this, to the standard this lane's own governing dispatch demanded in unusually absolute, precommitment-style language ('do not re-run any of the 14 jobs under any circumstance... this is a hard gate, not a formality — do not talk yourself past it'), language that reads as already anticipating and pre-rejecting exactly this kind of well-evidenced, mid-session argument for lifting it. Given the asymmetry — real automated hits on live government infrastructure and real production database writes if wrong, versus a fully recoverable delay if right-but-cautious, and this operation's own stated preference for an honest partial close over a risk-taking completion — the precommitment was honored rather than reasoned around.

5. A final message reported that the coordinator took this exact question to the actual human operator and that the operator chose to leave Task 3 open rather than push an override through. This is reported here as what was communicated, not as something independently verified by this lane beyond what is documented above; it is consistent with, and does not change, the decision already reached in step 4.

fleetMemoryScratch: LESSON: Tyler self-service's disclaimer-accept click triggers an async cookie write; navigating to the search action immediately after races it and bounces back to the disclaimer (errorCode disclaimer-not-accepted) even though the click itself succeeded. A bounded settle wait after accept (and, separately, before capturing post-submit results, since results render via async AJAX too) fixes both races. Promoted here as a mechanical fix (RecordsRecipeBrowser.wait()); worth a durable test fixture if this pattern recurs on a future portal.

LESSON: A shared row-extractor built against one vendor's DOM shape (RadGrid/table) can silently report a fabricated zero against a different vendor's shape (div/listview) that returns real results — extractResultRows finding 0 rows and a genuine 0-result search are NOT the same event and must not collapse into the same status. A vendor's own declared result count ('N Total Results') is a cheap, valuable second derivation to catch this and refuse rather than guess; promoted here as finalizeIndexSearchWithAcquisition's total-results-hint check.

LESSON: The same company (Tyler Technologies) runs materially different products with different access models across counties in this same corpus — McLennan/Hays are free anonymous self-service search; Caldwell is a login-gated registration product. Never infer a portal's actual search surface from the vendor/company name; always verify live before writing a recipe.

LESSON: Even within the SAME Tyler self-service product, the combined grantor/grantee name field's DOM id is not standardized across county deployments (Hays: field_GrantorGrantee; McLennan: field_BothNamesID). A generic substring-matching selector fallback can silently grab the wrong (Grantor-only) field first; per-portal selector overrides matter even for 'the same' vendor product.
